turns.text: Blood first — old, gone the color of rust in the concrete's pores, laid down by some argument that finished weeks before tonight started. Under it, colder and much closer: brine and fat, a hundred crates of tuna sweating through cold plastic behind a fence that ticks where the current runs live along it. Every guard's rotation on this stretch, every blind two minutes in the far camera's sweep, sits memorized already, the way an old wound stays memorized without needing a second look at it.

the restricted loading dock runs three bays deep under a floodlight grid that never fully goes dark, just dims on a cycle timed to something other than actual night. crates stack to the rafters behind chain-link humming low and constant, a guard booth glowing blue at the far end with nobody visibly awake inside it, and up on a charging rail bolted to the ceiling strut, a docked drone sits with its rotors folded, status light pulsing slow — asleep, or close enough to it. rain starts against the corrugated roof in scattered taps, building toward a rhythm it hasn't found yet.

The floodlight cycle dims on a four-count, same as always, and the guard booth's blue glow hasn't shifted in the time it's taken to count it twice. Now, then — while the light's low and the drone's rotors stay folded. Weight drops onto the balls of the paws, the old scar along one flank pulling tight the way it does before anything that matters.

the last stretch to the crates crosses open concrete laced with a grid of dull red lines, motion-tripped, crisscrossing at knee height and lower in a pattern that shifts every few minutes on its own schedule. near the third crate row a boot scuff shows fresh in a puddle, guard-sized, gone quiet again — whoever left it moved on already, bored, routine, not hunting. the red lines hold steady, patient, waiting on anything dumb enough to walk through them standing up.

Standing up was never the plan. Body flattens to nothing, belly dragging wet concrete, weaving the gaps between the red lines the way water finds gaps in a drain — not fast, not clever, just low enough that clever doesn't need to enter into it. One line brushes a whisker-tip and nothing sounds, which is the only proof any of this is working.

the last red line clears with room to spare, and the crates rise close now, cold radiating off the plastic wrap in a wall of brine-smell thick enough to taste before any of it's actually touched. the boot-scuff trail loops back this way once, pauses two rows over, then peels off toward the booth — not searching, just walking a beat that ends the same place every night. the chain-link's hum sits underneath everything, steady, unbothered.

The nearest crate's seam gives under claw and tooth both, plastic wrap tearing in one long ugly strip, cold biting straight through the gap into the nose before anything else registers — good cold, food cold, not storm cold. Jaw works at the strip, patient, pulling it wider one bite at a time instead of forcing it and making noise the fence would carry.

overhead, the charging rail's status light stutters off its slow pulse and holds solid — the drone's rotors unfold with a whine two full seconds ahead of any patrol schedule logged for this bay, off-cycle, unexplained, its single sensor eye swinging down toward the crate row on a straight, deliberate line.

/\/\_/\/\
    (  O   O  )
     \  ^Y^  /
      )=====(      -- ears up, rotor incoming --

Everything stops at once — jaw, breath, the strip of torn plastic still hanging from one tooth — body pressed so flat against the crate's cold flank that the fur takes on its texture. The rotor-whine reads first as pressure behind the ears, then as sound, then as a direction, and none of that changes what there is to do about it, which is nothing, which is stay exactly this still.

the drone's sweep clears the crate row a full body-length short, sensor-eye locked instead on a rat shape breaking cover three bays down, and it banks off that way with a burst of rotor-noise that fades fast under the roof's rain-tap. back on the rail, a second unit stays folded, undisturbed. the guard booth's blue glow doesn't flicker once through any of it. false alarm, filed and forgotten by whatever logged it.

The stillness breaks slow, one muscle at a time, tail last. Jaw finds the torn strip again, working it wider now with less patience than before, the near-miss still sitting cold in the chest the way the crate's cold sits against the flank. Enough. Get the crate open before anything else decides to reactivate.

from a speaker bolted crooked over the booth door, a broadcast bleeds through mid-sentence, forced-bright and looping — some cheer feed nobody down here asked for, a voice pitched too warm to be anything but manufactured, pushing a smile through what sounds like it wants to be a scream underneath the enthusiasm. it stutters once on a syllable, catches itself, keeps going. the fence keeps humming through it, unimpressed.

That warmth rings hollow the way it always does, a shape of a voice with none of the actual thing behind it, and it earns exactly the attention it deserves — none. Ears angle away from the speaker on their own, back toward the crate, toward the strip of plastic finally tearing free in one long piece. Hunger doesn't care what's playing overhead.

the cheer feed drags a beat lower, pitch souring off-key for two full seconds before it cuts out mid-word entirely, replaced without transition by a flatter tone — a bounty broadcast, corporate-clipped, chewing through a filing number and a reward figure too large to mean anything to anyone standing in the rain listening. it loops once, thins under the roof's static, and dies against the drum of rain finding its rhythm at last.

Numbers and filing tones are somebody else's weather, same as the cheer feed was, same as everything that comes out of that speaker ever is. The torn plastic finally gives its answer: a full brick of tuna, foil-backed, cold enough to numb the tongue on first contact and worth every red line crossed to get here. Teeth close on the corner and drag it back off the pallet edge.

rain thickens overhead, drumming the corrugated roof into something closer to noise than weather now, and across the dock's outer fence, up on the neighboring rooftop's ledge, a shape holds motionless against the skyline — narrow, upright, two flat discs where eyes should catch the floodlight and don't, reflecting it back instead. it doesn't move toward the fence. it doesn't move at all.

The mirrored shape gets one full look, held a beat longer than the drone earned, then let go the same way — not hunting this fence line, not claiming this dock, just another set of eyes doing its own version of tonight's business somewhere else entirely. The tuna brick weighs more than expected. Grip shifts to the middle for balance.

the ledge is empty on the next glance, no sound of a jump, no shift in the rain's pattern to mark a departure — just gone, the way that particular shape always seems to manage it. the red-line grid resets itself for its next cycle, indifferent to the torn crate three rows back. the guard booth's blue glow holds steady, and the folded drone on the rail settles its rotors back into sleep.

Retreat traces the same low line the approach did, red lines and all, weight kept off the wet concrete's loudest patches, tuna brick dragged rather than carried so the smell trails thin instead of thick — no sense leaving a wider mark on this fence than the crossing already did. The fence hums past overhead, unbothered, same note it started on.

past the fence line the alley swallows the dock's floodlight glow within thirty feet, rain finding its full rhythm at last against every surface at once, and the restricted loading dock settles back into its ordinary night — crates a little lighter than the manifest says, a torn strip of plastic already collecting rainwater, the bounty broadcast's echo long since rained out of the air. the city keeps its count elsewhere. this dock has already been counted for tonight.
